'''Jonathan Solomon Pila''' (born 1962)<ref name=whoswho/> is an Australian [[mathematician]] at the [[University of Oxford]]. He was awarded a BSc from the [[University of Melbourne]] in 1984, and a [[PhD]] from [[Stanford University]] in 1988, the latter for research supervised by [[Peter Sarnak]].<ref name="mathgene" /> His dissertation was entitled "Frobenius Maps of Abelian Varieties and Finding Roots of Unity in Finite Fields". In 2010, he received an MA from Oxford.<ref name="Oxford">{{cite web|url=http://www.maths.ox.ac.uk/people/profiles/jonathan.pila|title=Jonathan Pila|publisher=University of Oxford, Mathematical Institute|access-date=27 November 2011|archive-date=19 March 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120319010330/http://www.maths.ox.ac.uk/people/profiles/jonathan.pila|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Career and research==
Research interests lie in [[number theory]] and [[model theory]]. A focus has been applying the [[o-minimal theory|theory of o-minimality]] to [[Diophantine equation|Diophantine problems]]. This work began with an early paper with [[Enrico Bombieri]], and developed through collaborations with [[Alex Wilkie]] and [[Umberto Zannier]]. The techniques obtained have led to advances in Diophantine problems, including Pila's unconditional proof of the [[André–Oort conjecture]] for powers of the modular curve.<ref name=frs/> Work by Pila and [[Jacob Tsimerman]], demonstrated the André–Oort conjecture in the case of the [[Siegel modular form|Siegel modular variety]].<ref>{{cite journal|journal=Notices of the American Mathematical Society |title=February 2018 |issn=1088-9477 |volume=65 |issue=2 |year=2018 |page=191}}</ref>

Pila has held posts at [[Columbia University]], [[McGill University]], the [[University of Bristol]] and (as a visiting member) the [[Institute for Advanced Study]]. Pila also took a substantial break from professional mathematics to work in his family's manufacturing business.<ref name=frs/>

Pila has been the Editor of Proceedings of the ''[[Edinburgh Mathematical Society]]'', and of ''[[Algebra and Number Theory]]''.<ref name="Oxford"/>

==Awards and honours==
Pila was awarded a Clay Research Award for his work on the Andre-Oort conjecture in 2011<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.maths.ox.ac.uk/node/15208|title=Jonathan Pila receives a 2011 Clay Research Award|access-date=June 2, 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110530081126/http://www.maths.ox.ac.uk/node/15208 |archive-date=May 30, 2011 }}</ref>. In June 2011, he was awarded the [[Senior Whitehead Prize]]  by the [[London Mathematical Society]].<ref name="London">{{cite press release |url=http://www.lms.ac.uk/sites/default/files/About_Us/news/PR0511_LMSPrizes.pdf |title=London Mathematical Society Prizes 2011 |publisher=London Mathematical Society |access-date=27 November 2011}}</ref> This prize is "awarded in recognition of work in and influence on and service to mathematics; or lecturing gifts."<ref name="London"/> Specifically, the citation recognized "his startling recent work on the Andre-Oort and [[Manin-Mumford conjecture]]s. The approach he and his collaborators have developed, which combines analytic ideas with [[model theory]], is entirely new and shows great promise for further applications."<ref name="London"/> 

In addition to the Clay and London Mathematical Society awards, Pila delivered the [[Cahit Arf#Arf_Lectures|Arf Lecture]] in 2011, was awarded the Leverhulme Trust Research Fellowship 2008–2010.<ref name="Oxford"/> and received the [[Karp Prize]] in 2013.<ref>{{cite web|url = http://www.aslonline.org/info-prizes.html|title = Prizes and Awards|publisher = Association of Symbolic Logic|access-date = 27 August 2015|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20150828023729/http://www.aslonline.org/info-prizes.html|archive-date = 28 August 2015|url-status = dead|df = dmy-all}}</ref> Pila was elected a [[List of Fellows of the Royal Society elected in 2015|Fellow of the Royal Society (FRS) in 2015]].<ref name=frs/> In 2022, he received the [[Rolf Schock Prizes|Rolf Schock Prize]] in the category of "Mathematics".<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.kva.se/en/pressrum/pressmeddelanden/arkitekt-pianist-filosof-och-matematiker-far-arets-rolf-schockpriser |title=Rolf Schock Prize 2022 |access-date=24 March 2022 |archive-date=25 March 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220325075546/https://www.kva.se/en/pressrum/pressmeddelanden/arkitekt-pianist-filosof-och-matematiker-far-arets-rolf-schockpriser |url-status=dead }}</ref>
